claim: In a role trust policy, the sts:RoleSessionName condition key can require users to provide a specific session name when they assume a role, and the sts:SourceIdentity key can require them to set a specific source identity; an identity needs permission for the sts:SetSourceIdentity action to set a source identity.
question: Which condition keys in a role trust policy make users name their role session or set a source identity, and what extra permission does setting a source identity need?

values.display: require that your users provide a specific session name when they assume a role
require that your users set a specific source identity when they assume a role

qualifiers.scope: role trust policies (AWS STS condition keys)

evidence.quote: You can use this key in a role trust policy to require that your users provide a specific session name when they assume a role.
You can use this key in a role trust policy to require that your users set a specific source identity when they assume a role.
You must grant permissions for the `sts:SetSourceIdentity` action to allow an identity to set a source identity.

note: d085 (registrar follow-up search): the first sentence stands under the bold label sts:RoleSessionName, the second and third under sts:SourceIdentity on the same page.
